title: Retire six reference/name rules into unplaceable-reference
summary: Six writing rules — bare-reference, reference-without-label, reference-without-link, chat-local-reference, undefined-name and undefined-name-at-start — are deleted, and everything they caught is now reported by the single surviving rule unplaceable-reference. Because those ids are still written down in config files, suppression markers and osf-expect declarations, the change adds a RETIRED_RULE_IDS table and threads it through the three places an old id can appear: config loading (writing.levels and the removed writing.chat_local_labels key), the suppression engine, and expectation checking. Each of those now fails with a message naming unplaceable-reference instead of a silent no-op or a bare 'not a rule id'.

nodes.label: osf main
nodes.subtitle: explain, expectation_findings
nodes.summary: `osf explain` now short-circuits on a retired id and prints the replacement instead of 'no such rule'. `expectation_findings` gains a third bucket, `expectation-retired-rule`, alongside missing and unexpected.

nodes.label: verify
nodes.subtitle: declared_fixture_findings
nodes.summary: The pre-push fixture check passes RETIRED_RULE_IDS into check_expectation and renders retired declarations as their own error naming the replacement.

nodes.label: RETIRED_RULE_IDS
nodes.subtitle: &[(&str, &str)] — 6 pairs
nodes.summary: The single source of truth for the migration: each deleted rule id paired with unplaceable-reference. Read by config loading, the suppression engine, expectation checking and `osf explain`.

nodes.label: config::load
nodes.subtitle: removed_chat_local_labels_key, reject_retired_levels
nodes.summary: Two new guards run at load time: a config file still setting writing.chat_local_labels gets a message saying the key is gone and naming chat_local_phrases and must_explain_names; a writing.levels entry keyed by a retired rule id is refused with the replacement named.

nodes.label: WritingConfig
nodes.subtitle: chat_local_labels removed
nodes.summary: The chat_local_labels field, its default list and its OSF_WRITING_CHAT_LOCAL_LABELS env mapping are all deleted; the struct now carries only chat_local_phrases for conversation-local wording.

nodes.label: osf.toml
nodes.subtitle: must_explain_names comment
nodes.summary: The repository's own config file only updates a comment: the must-explain list is now described as feeding unplaceable-reference rather than undefined-name.

nodes.label: lint_writing
nodes.subtitle: apply_context, apply_suppressions
nodes.summary: The undefined_names pass is dropped from the pipeline, and apply_context no longer special-cases unplaceable-reference for evidence — every rule now resolves its level from its own finding's evidence. Suppression is called with RETIRED_RULE_IDS.

nodes.label: unplaceable-reference
nodes.subtitle: the surviving rule
nodes.summary: The one rule that now covers bare numbers, unlabelled and unlinked references, conversation-local phrases and labels, and undescribed names. Its behaviour is unchanged; it simply absorbs six rules' worth of findings.

nodes.label: 6 deleted rules
nodes.subtitle: bare-reference, reference-without-*, chat-local-reference, undefined-name*
nodes.summary: bare_reference, reference_without_label, ChatLocalRule, undefined_names and their rule_meta entries are removed from the rule set, the metadata table and rule_ids().

nodes.label: RULE_META
nodes.subtitle: 6 entries removed
nodes.summary: The metadata table loses the six retired entries, so `osf explain` and level resolution only know the surviving rules.

nodes.label: apply_suppressions
nodes.subtitle: validate_ids takes retired
nodes.summary: validate_ids now takes the retired table: an id that is not known but is retired still produces suppression-unknown-rule, but the message says it was replaced and names the replacement.

nodes.label: expectation::check
nodes.subtitle: Mismatch.retired
nodes.summary: check() takes retired_rules and returns a third bucket, retired: Vec<(old, new)>. A declared retired id is never folded into missing, and its replacement firing is not reported as unexpected.

nodes.label: writing fixtures
nodes.subtitle: osf-expect markers trimmed
nodes.summary: Fixture declarations drop the retired ids they used to name alongside unplaceable-reference, and the chat-local-named-label pair is deleted; the shape test's expected count drops from 32 to 30.

nodes.label: integration tests
nodes.subtitle: dsh, omp, opencode
nodes.summary: The three adapter test suites swap bare-reference for unplaceable-reference in their sample refusal strings; no adapter logic changes.

edges.label: explain + expectation_findings
edges.summary: The CLI's two new behaviours both read the same table: explain short-circuits on it, and expectation_findings turns its pairs into expectation-retired-rule errors.

edges.label: reject_retired_levels
edges.summary: Config loading consults the table so a writing.levels key naming a deleted rule fails loudly with the replacement named, rather than silently doing nothing.

edges.label: apply_suppressions(..., RETIRED_RULE_IDS)
edges.summary: The writing pipeline now hands the retired table to the suppression engine so a marker naming an old id explains itself.
The surviving rule is invoked exactly as before; what changed is that nothing else runs beside it.

edges.label: undefined_names, per_sentence rules
edges.summary: The undefined_names pass and the sentence-level bare-reference and reference-without-label rules are no longer invoked.
Level and remediation still come from the metadata table, now resolved against the finding's own evidence for every rule.

edges.label: check_expectation(..., RETIRED_RULE_IDS)
edges.summary: The pre-push fixture check passes the retired table through and renders the retired bucket as its own error.

edges.label: check_expectation(..., RETIRED_RULE_IDS)
edges.summary: The in-process fixture check in main.rs does the same, producing expectation-retired-rule findings.

edges.label: osf-expect markers
edges.summary: Fixture declarations no longer name the retired ids, so the expectation check sees only unplaceable-reference.
The repository's own config file is still read by the loader; only a comment changed.
The loader still produces WritingConfig, now without chat_local_labels and with retired level keys rejected before they land.

edges.label: refusal reason strings
edges.summary: Adapter tests assert on the CLI's rendered rule id, so they move to unplaceable-reference with no adapter code change.

flows.title: A stale retired rule id meets the new guards
flows.summary: Three entry points where a deleted rule id can still be written down, and how each now answers with the replacement.

messages.label: writing.levels.undefined-name-at-start = "off"
messages.note: reject_retired_levels scans the levels map against RETIRED_RULE_IDS before the config is accepted.

messages.label: error: the rule is gone; use writing.levels.unplaceable-reference
<!-- osf-disable-line bare-reference -- tracked -->
messages.note: The marker is still an error, but validate_ids now looks the id up in the retired table first.

messages.label: osf-expect: bare-reference
messages.note: check() splits the declared id into the retired bucket instead of missing.

messages.label: osf explain bare-reference → run `osf explain unplaceable-reference`
messages.note: Exit code 0, not the old 'no such rule' error on stderr.

views.title: Rule retirement and the migration guards
views.summary: The six deleted rules collapse into unplaceable-reference, and RETIRED_RULE_IDS is the table the CLI, config loader and expectation checker all read to tell a stale id where to go.

views.title: Config loading guards
views.summary: The two new checks in config::load: the removed chat_local_labels key and a writing.levels entry naming a retired rule.

views.title: Expectation checking path
views.summary: How a declared fixture's rule ids reach check(), and how the retired bucket becomes its own error in both the CLI and verify.

steps.heading: Six rules deleted
steps.body: bare-reference, the two reference-without-* rules, chat-local-reference and both undefined-name rules leave the rule set.

steps.heading: One table records the migration
steps.body: RETIRED_RULE_IDS pairs each deleted id with unplaceable-reference, the rule that now covers it.

steps.heading: Config refuses stale keys
steps.body: A writing.levels entry or the removed chat_local_labels key now fails with the replacement named.

steps.heading: Declarations name the replacement
steps.body: A fixture declaring a retired id gets expectation-retired-rule instead of a bare 'did not fire'.

steps.heading: Three ways a stale id surfaces
steps.body: Config, suppression marker and osf-expect declaration each answer with unplaceable-reference.
